text:
Boston needed a shootout to beat Vegas, and only one shooter in six attempts found the net: David Pastrnak, who scored in the third round after Carter Hart and Jeremy Swayman had stopped everyone else. Pastrnak, drafted 25th overall by the Bruins in 2014, also led the night in effort, putting seven shots on goal and picking up an assist on Morgan Geekie's power-play goal.

That goal was the odd one. Geekie scored on a chance our model gave only a 3% shot of going in, and it put BOS up 2-0 early in the second period. VGK pushed back hard from there. Over the second period they out-chanced the Bruins 1.46 to 0.63 in expected goals, a measure of the quality of shots taken. Mark Stone cut the lead on the power play, and Trevor Connelly tied it in the third on another low-odds wrist shot, a 4% look set up by Noah Hanifin and Mitch Marner. Marner, the fourth overall pick in 2015, finished with two assists and ran the offense for 24 minutes.

Over the full game, though, the Bruins had the better of it. They took 60 shot attempts to 49 and edged expected goals 2.83 to 2.67, which gives them a 53% chance of winning if we replayed every shot. BOS also drew the better power-play looks, 1.08 expected goals to 0.81, while VGK took 19 penalty minutes to Boston's 6. Both goalies came out slightly ahead of expectation, Hart by 0.83 goals and Swayman by 0.67. Our facts don't include streaks or records for either side, so the result stands as a close one that Boston narrowly deserved.
